hook.text: In some cities, switching from bus to train means paying a second fare. Riders hate it.

buildup.text: Fare integration means one ticket or card covers all modes—bus, tram, metro, commuter rail.

discovery.text: London's Oyster card and daily caps let riders transfer freely without worrying about extra charges.

twist.text: Integrated fares require cooperation between competing operators. Political turf wars often block it.

climax.text: Cities with seamless fare integration consistently have higher ridership than fragmented ones.

punchline.text: One card, all modes, no penalty. Ridership follows.

quiz.question: What is fare integration?
options: One ticket covers all transit modes without double charging
